name: Do I need permits to remodel a kitchen in Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in Los Angeles if I am not moving walls?
mainEntity.text: Do I need a permit to remodel a kitchen in Los Angeles if I am not moving walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permits are often required when a kitchen remodel changes plumbing, electrical, gas, ventilation, or structure. A cosmetic update such as replacing cabinet doors, countertops, paint, or flooring may be simpler, but once the work involves moving a sink, adding new circuits, changing gas lines, altering the vent hood, or opening walls, permit requirements usually increase. In the Los Angeles area, different cities can have different review processes, so homeowners should confirm the plan before demolition starts. The safest approach is to have the contractor identify which parts of the scope need permit review and which do not. This matters because unpermitted work can create inspection problems, delay the project, and complicate resale. Homeowners should ask for a permit strategy before signing a contract, including who prepares drawings, who submits the plans, and who handles inspections. That clarity prevents expensive surprises once construction begins.
